sequenceName: Equitas SFB Screener Part 2 - Edit Decision List

events.name: The Profit Collapse
events.facecamPosition: 0-90: Full Screen -> 90-240: Left (x: 60px, y: 50px, w: 580px, h: 980px, r: 24px)
events.leadDialogue: Why did the profit tipped so drastically? Many retail investors would have thought the bank is collapsing, right?
events.visualFocus: FY24 ₹799 Cr vs Mid-2025 -₹224 Cr drop, Retail sentiment dilemma

events.name: The Smart Investor Looks Deeper
events.leadDialogue: But here is what the smart investor would do little different stuff. If you read the conference called Transcript...
events.visualFocus: Official Q2 FY25 Concall Transcript extract, forensic due diligence highlight

events.name: The Microfinance Crisis
events.leadDialogue: ...the reason was very specific, the Indian microfinance crisis. Across India, Lender has flooded the rural and semi-urban borrowers with microfinance loans.
events.visualFocus: Multi-lender credit flow diagram converging on rural households

events.name: One Borrower, Multiple Loans
events.leadDialogue: A single borrower was taking four to five different loans simultaneously.
events.visualFocus: 5 simultaneous loan cards stacked, Debt trap: ₹17,100 EMI vs ₹15,000 income

events.name: Regional Stress & Heatwaves
events.leadDialogue: When a regional stress hit in a place like Karnataka and heat waves disrupted the rural wages, defaults exploded. Across the entire microfinance industry.
events.visualFocus: Karnataka collection friction card + Severe summer heatwaves wage disruption card

events.name: The Credit Cost Shock
events.leadDialogue: In equitas, microfinance credit cost shot up from 2.3% in FI-24 to a staggering 11.37% in FI-25.

events.name: The ₹630 Crore Impact
events.leadDialogue: That single segment wiped out over 630 crores of operating profits.
events.visualFocus: -₹630 Cr operating profit wipeout hero metric, Rubber stamp: CONTAINED TO MFI

events.name: Did Management Hide Bad Loans?
events.leadDialogue: Now, let's look what management actually did. Did they try to hide their bad loans? No, not actually.
events.visualFocus: Governance comparison: Evergreening trap vs Radical transparency

events.name: Action 01: Honesty & Clean-up
events.leadDialogue: Number one, what they did is they were completely honest. In mid 2025, they accepted a big loss of 224 crores. They cleaned up all their bad loans in one go instead of hiding the problem for years as a backlog.
events.visualFocus: -₹224 Cr loss card, Rubber stamp: CLEANED IN ONE GO

events.name: Action 02: Stricter Lending
events.leadDialogue: Point number two, they became very strict. If someone already had too many loans, the bank simply said no for the new loans.
events.visualFocus: Underwriting decision engine, Red gate: LOAN DECLINED

events.name: 50% Risky Applications Rejected
events.leadDialogue: In fact, they rejected almost half of the risky borrowers loan request. They chose safety over the risky growth.
events.visualFocus: ~50% rejection rate hero stat, Safety over reckless growth trade-off

events.name: 15% vs 85% Portfolio Insight
events.leadDialogue: And point number three is overall in 100% of the business, only 15% is actually attributed to this risk.
events.visualFocus: SVG doughnut chart: 15% Stressed MFI vs 85% Secured Core Lending

events.name: The 85% Asset-Backed Lending Business
events.leadDialogue: 85% of the total lending is backed by the real asset like property, shops and commercial vehicles.
events.visualFocus: 3 Physical Asset Pillars: Mortgages/LAP, Commercial Vehicles, Kirana Shops

events.name: Repayment Discipline
events.leadDialogue: In this main business, almost everyone pays the EMI properly on time.
events.visualFocus: Monthly EMI Calendar Grid (Jan-Dec) with 12 animated emerald checkmarks

events.name: Final Portfolio Perspective
events.leadDialogue: Only that small microfinancing part was hurting them and they fixed it.
events.visualFocus: Forensic verdict glassmorphism banner, Teaser to Part 3 Phoenix Rebound
